references.text: Jesus' prediction about Peter's denial, which Peter now remembers: 'The rooster will not crow today before you have denied knowing me three times' ([ref:Luk 22:34|Luke 22:34]).
Matthew's parallel account of Peter remembering Jesus' words and going out to weep bitterly ([ref:Matt 26:75|Matthew 26:75]).
Mark's parallel account of Peter's denial and his recollection of Jesus' prediction ([ref:Mark 14:72|Mark 14:72]).
John's account of Peter's third denial and the rooster's crowing ([ref:Joh 18:27|John 18:27]).
Jesus' prediction in John's Gospel that the rooster will not crow before Peter has denied him three times ([ref:Joh 13:38|John 13:38]).
Jesus' prediction in Matthew about Peter's denial: 'Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times' ([ref:Matt 26:34|Matthew 26:34]).
Jesus' prediction in Mark about Peter's denial, where the rooster crows twice ([ref:Mark 14:30|Mark 14:30]).
The full account of Peter's three denials in the courtyard of the high priest's house, which forms the immediate context for Jesus' look toward Peter ([ref:Luk 22:54-62|Luke 22:54–62]).
After the resurrection, Jesus restores Peter by asking him three times if he loves him—a restoration that mirrors the three denials ([ref:Joh 21:15-17|John 21:15–17]).

Jesus had predicted that Satan would sift Peter like wheat, but that He had prayed for him so that his faith would not fail—the Lord's intercession behind the compassionate look ([ref:Luk 22:31-32|Luke 22:31–32]).
